The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

rationales.general:
1. Ask what stood near St. Augustine. Fort Caroline, built by French Protestants in 1564.
2. Ask what Spain did. Spanish forces destroyed Fort Caroline in 1565 and built St. Augustine at once.
3. Ask why a fort, not a town. Spain needed soldiers on the Florida coast to hold it against a rival empire.
4. Rule out the others. Florida had no gold, Spain did not trade furs there, and Potosi silver sailed from Havana.
Remember: when a settlement is a fort first, ask which rival it was built against.
rationales.B: Spain fortified Florida to block French Protestant colonization and secure its imperial claims. Fort Caroline, built by French Huguenots in 1564, was destroyed by Spain in 1565.
rationales.A: Potosi silver shipped through Caribbean ports and Havana, not through Florida. St. Augustine was not a silver port.
rationales.C: Florida held no gold deposits. The gold Spain sought lay in Mexico and Peru, not on the Florida coast.
rationales.D: Spain's model in Florida rested on missions and military control, not on fur-trading partnerships with Native peoples.

stem: Spain founded St. Augustine, Florida, in 1565 — the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States. Which broader development best explains why Spain established a fortified settlement there at that time?

stimulus.source_note: Original summary; Fort Caroline built 1564 by French Huguenots under Laudonniere, destroyed by Menendez 1565; St. Augustine founded 1565.
stimulus.text: Spanish forces destroyed the French Fort Caroline in 1565 and immediately established the fortified town of St. Augustine on the Florida coast.
